answer.evidence: This is a car, not a box, so the kind only loosely matches. The roof is a lighter band at rows 6-16 that ends in a dark edge line at row 17, followed by darker window rows 18-24. The trunk and hood are lighter blue plates at rows 13-24 that also read as top surfaces. Below them is the vertical body side at rows 25-41, with two wheels and door seams. The red taillight on the left and the yellow headlight on the right put the car facing east. The silhouette widens from 21 to 74 px over rows 5-14, consistent with a top surface above a south-facing side.

styleAnswer.evidence: The blue car reads clearly, but its main body panels use only about 3 lightness steps (one base blue, a lighter top highlight, a darker lower shade). The windows are flat blue with a single highlight streak. The outline is a dark, near-neutral line around nearly every shape (89% of dark edge pixels are neutral). This is the sticker look, whereas Beodeul outlines are tinted to the adjacent material (stall 1%, hedge 0%). The body, roof and door panels are large smooth fills with no grain, speckle or per-panel texture. 14% near-flat coverage is similar to the cheese stall (13%), but those areas are designed fills there. At 9 visible tones per tile the car matches the hedge but falls well below the stall (17) and the well (20), which carry much more material variety. The shading is shallow, the outline is near-black, and the surfaces are flat, so it does not match the Beodeul standard.
